fields.label: Is the client using less than 1 teaspoon (5g) of salt per day?

fields.text:
"Reducing Salt Intake"
▪b Target: less than 1 teaspoon (5g) per day
▪ Eating too much salt can raise your blood pressure, increase your risk of heart disease, and make it harder to control your blood sugar.

Tap ⓘ for the full counselling guide
fields.toaster_info_text:
What to do: Limit salt intake to protect your heart and blood sugar control

Why: Too much salt raises blood pressure, increases risk of heart disease, and can worsen diabetes control

When: Every day, with every meal and snack

Where: At home and when eating out, be mindful of hidden salt in processed and restaurant foods

How: Keep salt below 5 grams (1 teaspoon) per day, avoid adding extra salt, choose fresh foods, read labels, and use herbs and spices for flavor instead

fields.label: Is the client using less than 5 teaspoons of sugar per day?

fields.text:
"Reducing Sugar Intake"
▪ Target: less than 5 teaspoons per day
▪ Too much sugar raises blood sugar levels, increases the risk of diabetes complications, and harms heart health.

Tap ⓘ for the full counselling guide
fields.toaster_info_text:
What to do: Limit sugar intake to control blood sugar and protect your health

Why: Too much sugar raises blood sugar levels, increases the risk of diabetes complications, and harms heart health

When: Every day, with all meals and drinks

Where: At home and when eating out. Watch for hidden sugars in drinks, snacks, and processed foods.

How: Keep added sugar as low as possible, avoid sugary drinks and sweets, choose water or unsweetened drinks, eat whole foods, and read food labels of processed foods and drinks.

fields.label: Does the client exercise for at least 30 minutes per day until sweating?

fields.text:
"Increasing Physical Activity"
▪ Target: at least 30 minutes per day, until sweating
▪ Exercise helps lower blood pressure, control blood sugar, strengthen the heart, and maintain a healthy weight.

Tap ⓘ for the full counselling guide
fields.toaster_info_text:
What to do: Engage in regular physical exercise to improve your health

Why: Exercise helps lower blood pressure, control blood sugar, strengthen the heart, and maintain a healthy weight

When: At least 30 minutes most days of the week

Where: At home, outdoors, or any safe place convenient for you

How: Start with simple activities like walking, cycling, or stretching, increase gradually, and stay consistent

fields.label: Is the client avoiding alcohol or drinking within safe limits?

fields.text:
"Reducing Alcohol Intake"
▪ Target: avoid alcohol; if drinking, no more than 2 standard drinks per day for men or 1 for women
▪ Alcohol raises blood pressure, worsens diabetes control, damages the liver and heart, and can interact with medicines.

Tap ⓘ for the full counselling guide
fields.toaster_info_text:
What to do: Avoid alcohol or keep intake within safe limits to protect heart, blood pressure, and blood sugar control

Why: Alcohol raises blood pressure, can cause low blood sugar (especially with diabetes medicines), damages the liver and heart, adds empty calories, and increases the risk of stroke and cancer. WHO advises that less is better, and none is best.

When: There is no safe daily amount; if drinking occasionally, keep it to no more than 2 standard drinks per day for men or 1 for women, and have several alcohol-free days each week

Where: At home and at social events. Be aware of pressure to drink and prepare polite refusals.

How: Set a personal limit (or aim for none), choose water or unsweetened drinks, do not drink on an empty stomach (especially if on diabetes medicines), and seek help if cutting down is difficult

fields.label: Is the client free from tobacco use (smoking and smokeless)?

fields.text:
"Stopping Tobacco Use"
▪ Target: complete cessation — no smoking and no smokeless tobacco
▪ Tobacco damages blood vessels, raises blood pressure, worsens diabetes complications, and is a leading cause of heart disease, stroke, and cancer.

Tap ⓘ for the full counselling guide
fields.toaster_info_text:
What to do: Stop all forms of tobacco — cigarettes, pipes, shisha, and smokeless tobacco like snuff or chewing tobacco. Avoid second-hand smoke at home and work.

Why: Tobacco raises blood pressure, damages blood vessels, accelerates diabetes complications (kidney, eye, foot, and heart problems), and is a leading cause of heart disease, stroke, lung disease, and many cancers. There is no safe level of tobacco use.

When: Quit as soon as possible — stopping at any age improves health within days, weeks, and years

Where: Make home and workplace tobacco-free; ask family and friends not to smoke around the client

How: Set a quit date, remove tobacco products from the environment, identify and avoid triggers, drink water or take a short walk when cravings hit (they usually pass within minutes), and seek support from the health facility or cessation services — brief advice from a health worker doubles the chance of success
